title: I built and soon release a Steam game using Codex/GPT-6 Astra — here's my workflow and what I learned
author: Baumbeard
selftext:
I recently published an article about my experience developing and releasing my first Steam game, Azzog's Idle Asteroid, using Codex/GPT-6 Astra.

I wanted to go beyond the usual "look what AI made" posts and share what actually goes into building and shipping a game with AI coding agents.

Some of the topics I cover:

\- How I organize project knowledge using AGENTS.md and other Markdown files to keep AI agents on track

\- Why iterative development works better for me than giant one-shot prompts

\- How Git and structured documentation help manage an AI-assisted codebase

\- Where AI helped me overcome limitations as a solo developer

\- The challenges that AI doesn't magically solve, from game design to actually releasing on Steam

I also share some thoughts on AI-assisted development as a new abstraction layer in programming and the criticism surrounding AI-generated games.

Here's the full article:

https://medium.com/@azzogs.asteroid/ai-game-development-with-codex-gpt-6-astra-2efba1dde80a

I'd love to hear how other AI game developers approach this.

Are you mostly using AI for specific tasks, or have you moved toward letting coding agents handle large parts of your development workflow? And what's been your biggest bottleneck?

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body:
My biggest bottle neck is 1. $20 plan usage and 2.  Hand made level creation. Mines a rogue like where you only see 8 levels per floor per run but I have to make about 25 since the keys don’t always connect to each (since the levels are meant to merge seamlessly) but also having to go back and polish thing or seeing bugs in testing ect is why I’m 7 months in (only an hour a day on average so like being 1 or two months in full time on 5x plan) and I don’t have a single playable floor yet (I am targeting a playable floor for me in 2 weeks and a playable demo with two floors this year, there will be 6 floors)

comments.author: Fun-Term616
comments.body:
The biggest bottle neck is when ai doesn't make something quality and we have to break down the task smaller and smaller until AI can do. 

Here is an example I want my own custom animations. Specifically I want a Macho Man Flying Elbow animation. No text to motion or video to motion AI is capable of making that animation. Cartwheel gets the closest. Okay let's break down the problem to something smaller, have the animation broken down into four different segments. Text to animation, start to finish image reference ai, motion smaller and smaller segments until the motion is quality. Now you have a process for making quality animations and you have a prompt for how you want AI to work. It takes a long time to break down tasks but AI can do everything, you just have process in place to ensure.
